admission.capacity: driver free plus allocator cached-unallocated capacity; do not count currently allocated banks as free
admission.live_and_future_accounting: future bank bytes decrease as saved upward and direct-gradient blocks materialize; after direct bank is complete, later release reduces the live requirement without reserving another future bank
admission.repeat_checks: after first forward blocks and at backward boundaries

change: Save detached first-sweep upward blocks on the existing compute device, without CPU copies or a full concatenated bank. Reuse the exact qualified first_device and forcing_device helpers.

The inherited second sweep accepts its upward leaf on device. Its direct upward gradient therefore remains on device, while readout derivatives, final context and decoder context VJP retain CPU interfaces.

Accumulate direct upward plus forcing upward gradients in the original direct-first order on device and consume that owned block in the original first-sweep VJP. Preserve all-second-reversed, full-history-theta, then per-block forcing followed by first parameter contribution order.

Both upward and direct-gradient banks exist across the full stable_leaf_history_v2 backward. Direct-gradient storage releases blockwise after first VJP; autograd retains upward until backward returns. No attempt is made to claim premature saved-tensor release.

Actual native layout/node count gives exact payloads. A scalar ledger validates contiguous FP32 private storage, no aliases/hidden larger backing banks, full two-bank history lifetime and one release per direct block. It stores no tensor references.
limits: CPU parity validates algebra, ownership and state accounting; it cannot prove CUDA parity, allocator behavior, throughput or full-parent peak.

Moving the upward leaf and its accumulated derivative to CUDA changes cross-device autograd placement. The real observed1153-prefix qualification must compare every49 gradient, parameter and Adam state before any full-parent claim.

The sixteen-GiB scratch allowance is an explicit operational allowance, not a theorem for history, decoder, temporary first graph, allocator fragmentation or library workspaces. Full-parent measured qualification remains required.
Driver/allocator snapshots are sequential and cached capacity is not a promise of contiguous reusable storage; an allocation error is fatal, with no reduced workload fallback.
First-sweep recomputation is inherited from boundary fusion and still depends on that candidate CUDA qualification.
No second retained full-bank copy is introduced; transient single-block graph/gradient tensors remain and belong to scratch.
